GROUND LEASE COVENANTS (Para 32, p.17): Trustor must pay all Ground Lease rents when due and perform all tenant obligations; Trustor shall NOT, without Beneficiary's prior consent, surrender, terminate, cancel, modify or supplement the Ground Lease — any such act without consent 'shall be void and of no force and effect'; Beneficiary may cure Trustor's Ground Lease defaults at Default Rate and is subrogated to Ground Lessor; Trustor must exercise Ground Lease renewal/extension options on Beneficiary's demand (irrevocable POA granted); Trustor will not subordinate the Ground Lease to any interest in Ground Lessor's fee

GROUND LEASE SUBLEASES (Para 33, p.17): every future Lease/renewal must be non-terminable if the Ground Lease terminates and Beneficiary enters a new ground lease with Ground Lessor, or upon foreclosure (unless tenant named and joined); tenants must attorn to foreclosure purchaser
NO MERGER (Para 34, p.18): fee title and leasehold estate shall not merge while Debt unpaid absent Beneficiary written consent

TRUSTOR'S ACQUISITION OF FEE (Para 35, p.18): if Trustor becomes owner of fee title, Trustor must subject the fee to the lien of this DoT and deliver updated title policy insuring first lien on the fee — critical unwind mechanic

BANKRUPTCY / 365(h) (Para 36, p.18): no election to treat Ground Lease terminated without Beneficiary consent; lien extends to Trustor's possessory rights and rejection-damage claims; Trustor assigns 365 rights to Beneficiary; at Beneficiary's request Trustor must assign its Ground Lease interest to Beneficiary in lieu of rejection; if Ground Lease terminates and Beneficiary/designee gets a new lease, Trustor has no interest in it (Para 36(d), p.19)

TRANSFER PROHIBITION (Para 4, pp.6-7): no sale, conveyance, mortgage, encumbrance, pledge or Transfer of the Trust Property other than a 'Permitted Transfer' (defined in Loan Agreement); violation = Debt immediately due, transfer null and void; no impairment showing required

LOAN REPAYMENT / RELEASE (Para 24, p.15): 'Provided no Event of Default exists, the Lien of this Deed of Trust shall be terminated, released and reconveyed of record by Beneficiary...prior to the Maturity Date only in accordance with the terms and provisions set forth in the Loan Agreement'

DEFEASANCE/ASSIGNMENT MECHANIC (p.5): upon payment in full, automatic reconveyance; or at Trustor's request, Beneficiary shall assign the DoT and endorse the Note 'to a lender designated by Trustor' without representation, warranty or recourse — useful for refi/unwind without lien release

INTEREST RATE PROTECTION (Para 31, pp.16-17): Trustor is or may be party to an Interest Rate Protection Agreement; default thereunder is an Event of Default; Trustor's rights assigned via Collateral Assignment of Interest Rate Protection Agreement of even date (2/27/2025); Beneficiary advances under it accrue at Default Rate and are secured

EXCULPATION (Para 27, p.15): Trustor liability limited pursuant to Section 10.1 of the Loan Agreement (non-recourse carve-out structure lives in the Loan Agreement)
GOVERNING LAW (Para 26, p.15): Texas law for creation/perfection/enforcement of the DoT; New York law for all other matters, the Loan Documents, and the Debt

TEXAS PROVISIONS (Paras 37-38, pp.19-22): Tex. Prop. Code 51.002 foreclosure mechanics; waiver of deficiency-statute FMV protections (51.003-51.005) to extent permitted; TARA (Ch. 64) assignment of rents; DTPA waiver; entire-agreement (statute of frauds) notice; jury trial waiver (Para 22, p.14)

key_terms: DIRECTION OF OPTION: The Owner/lessee does NOT hold a repurchase option in this document. The Owner (Grantor) grants Pleasanton HFC (Grantee) the Option to purchase the Project; the HFC also gets the Refusal Right. Any lessee-side right to reacquire the fee would be in the Ground Lease ('except as otherwise set forth in the Ground Lease' appears in both Sec. 1.a and Sec. 3).
Option (Sec. 1.a, p.2): during the Ground Lease term, HFC may purchase the Project on any date 45 days after delivering notice of intent to Owner and each of its members.

Option Purchase Price (Sec. 2.a, p.2) = (I) Fair Market Value of land and improvements PLUS (II) the 'Owner Diminution': (i) after-tax diminution of economic value to Owner's members, including without limitation (A) 125% of aggregate capital contributions and any other advances made by the partners of the Tenant prior to closing; (B) outstanding balance of all loans (plus accrued interest and yield maintenance) made to Owner by its members/affiliates or the guarantors and any other lenders not otherwise repaid at purchase; (C) any accrued and unpaid fees owed to Owner or its affiliates; and (ii) all unreimbursed costs/expenses of Owner's investors re (A) admission to the joint venture, (B) pre-purchase Project activities, (C) an amount sufficient for limited investors to pay, after taxes on the distribution, the taxes projected from the sale. FMV determined in accordance with the Partnership Agreement.

FMV / appraisal mechanics (Sec. 2.b, pp.2-3): FMV considers recorded land-use restrictions and third-party liens AND ASSUMES ANY PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION REMAINS WITH THE PROJECT; independent appraiser agreed by Grantee and Sponsor Member; failing agreement each picks one and the two appoint a third; three appraisers each determine FMV within 30 days of the third's appointment; FMV = average of the three, except any determination more than 10% above/below the average is disregarded; if none differs from the average by more than 10%, FMV = the MIDDLE determination. Each party pays its own appraiser; jointly selected appraiser fees split equally between Grantee and Sponsor Member.

Equity-purchase alternative (Sec. 2.c, p.3): 'Grantee may, at its option, exercise the Option described in this section by acquiring all of the equity interests of the Sponsor Members. Such purchase price will be paid by Grantee to Grantor in exchange for an assignment of the interest.'

ROFR triggers (Sec. 3, p.3): applies (provided Managing Member has not been removed/withdrawn from Owner) when Sponsor Member receives an acceptable bona fide third-party Offer to purchase (a) the unencumbered fee estate and termination of the Ground Lease, (b) all interests of Sponsor Member in the Grantor, or (c) an assignment of Grantor's rights under the Ground Lease. Grantee gets an irrevocable, exclusive right of first refusal at terms not less favorable than the Offer; 30 days to exercise after written notice; 90 days from receipt of Offer to close.
ROFR governmental-status condition (Sec. 3, p.3): the Refusal Right is effective only if Grantee is a governmental agency in good standing on both the exercise date and the closing date.

ROFR burn-off (Sec. 3, p.3): if not exercised or not closed on time, no subsequent change in Offer terms reinstates it EXCEPT a price reduction of more than 10% from the original Offer; Sponsor Member then has 12 months (starting day 31 after Grantee's receipt of the Offer) to consummate; failure to consummate reinstates the Refusal Right; consummation within 12 months TERMINATES both the Option and the Refusal Right permanently. Owner not obligated to reimburse Managing Member for costs (incl. attorney fees) of a sale to the Grantee entity under the Refusal Right.

Conditions precedent to exercise (Sec. 4.a, p.4): at exercise and purchase (i) neither Grantee nor any affiliate in material default past notice/cure under the Operating Agreement or any agreement with Owner or Investment Member; (ii) Grantee or affiliate must still be MAJORITY OWNER OF THE MANAGING MEMBER of Owner (except as provided in 'Section 5.b.(iv)' [apparent cross-reference error for 4.b.(iv)]); (iii) Grantee must be a housing finance corporation. If unsatisfied, the rights are not exercisable and the Agreement is of no further force or effect.

Automatic termination (Sec. 4.b, p.4): (i) transfer of the Project to any lender holding a security interest (foreclosure, deed in lieu or otherwise) in total or partial satisfaction of Project debt; (ii) Project ceases to meet the restrictions in the Regulatory Agreement and Declaration of Restrictive Covenants between Grantee and Grantor; (iii) any transfer or attempted transfer of all or part of the Refusal Right except as permitted; (iv) removal of Managing Member as managing member of Owner under the Operating Agreement — but auto-reinstated if within 30 days Grantee (1) satisfies all payment obligations to Sponsor Member and other members in full and (2) pays all costs/expenses (incl. reasonable attorney's fees) of the removal/replacement and correction of Project issues arising from Managing Member's acts/omissions; (v) Grantee's acquisition of legal title to the Project.

Contract and closing (Sec. 5.a, pp.4-5): on Option exercise, written PSA with closing within 60 days of exercise notice (extendable up to 30 more days if diligently pursuing); absent a contract the Agreement is specifically enforceable upon exercise. ROFR closing per the Offer terms.

Conveyance (Sec. 5.b, p.5): warranty deed ('Deed'), blanket conveyance/bill of sale/assignment ('Bill of Sale'), and assignment of Owner's interests under the Ground Lease ('Ground Lease Assignment') = 'Conveyance Documents'; Owner delivers, at Grantee's cost, a Texas form Owner's Title Policy in the amount of the purchase price. unwind_relevant: CRITICAL STRUCTURE POINT: This document does NOT give the Owner/lessee an option to buy the fee back from Pleasanton HFC. The option runs HFC-ward: the HFC (Grantee) holds the Option to buy the Project from the Owner, plus a ROFR over sponsor-side exits. Both Sec. 1.a and Sec. 3 carve out 'except as otherwise set forth in the Ground Lease' — the lessee's fee-repurchase/Ground Lease termination mechanics, if any, must be located in the recorded Ground Lease, which should be pulled and read for the actual unwind price.

PATH TO COLLAPSE THE PFC VIA SALE (Sec. 3): a sale of (a) the unencumbered fee estate WITH termination of the Ground Lease, (b) all of Sponsor Member's interests in the Grantor, or (c) an assignment of Grantor's rights under the Ground Lease is expressly contemplated — each is an 'Offer' event subject to the HFC's ROFR. Process cost: give HFC written notice with full Offer terms; HFC has 30 days to exercise and 90 days from receipt to close; if HFC passes or fails to close, Sponsor Member has 12 months (from day 31 after HFC's receipt) to consummate at terms not reduced in price by more than 10%; CONSUMMATION WITHIN THAT WINDOW PERMANENTLY TERMINATES BOTH THE OPTION AND THE ROFR — i.e., a completed third-party sale run through the ROFR gauntlet cleanly extinguishes the HFC's rights under this Agreement.

HFC OPTION PRICE IF HFC EXERCISES (Sec. 2): FMV of land+improvements (appraised assuming the property-tax exemption REMAINS with the Project) PLUS 'Owner Diminution' — including 125% of all partner capital contributions/advances, full repayment of member/affiliate/guarantor loans with accrued interest and yield maintenance, accrued unpaid fees, unreimbursed investor costs, and a tax gross-up for limited investors. This formula makes an HFC-side buyout expensive and sponsor-protective; it is not a bargain-purchase right.

ADDITIONAL HFC EXERCISE COSTS (Sec. 5.c): on any HFC exercise, Grantee bears ALL closing costs — transfer taxes, exit taxes, Sponsor Member's income taxes, loan prepayment/breakage, recording — plus a 4% broker commission payable to Sponsor Member; Grantee must also replace or release all sponsor-side Guarantors (Sec. 5.d).

TERMINATION TRIGGERS THAT KILL THE HFC'S RIGHTS AUTOMATICALLY (Sec. 4.b): (i) lender foreclosure/deed-in-lieu transfer of the Project; (ii) Project ceasing to meet the Regulatory Agreement and Declaration of Restrictive Covenants (note: exiting the regulatory regime terminates the HFC's option/ROFR — but presumably also the tax exemption); (iii) prohibited transfer of the Refusal Right; (iv) removal of PHFC SLH MM, LLC as managing member (subject to the HFC's 30-day cure/reinstatement by paying all obligations and removal costs); (v) HFC acquiring title. Also Sec. 8: the Agreement terminates on any transfer by foreclosure or deed in lieu under the LoanCore loan.

CONDITIONS THAT DISABLE THE HFC'S RIGHTS (Sec. 4.a): the Option/ROFR are exercisable only while (i) Grantee/affiliates are not in uncured material default, (ii) Grantee or an affiliate remains MAJORITY OWNER of Owner's managing member, and (iii) Grantee is a housing finance corporation; the ROFR additionally requires Grantee to be a governmental agency in good standing at exercise AND closing (Sec. 3). If unsatisfied, 'the Refusal Right and/or Options shall not be exercisable and this Agreement shall be of no further force or effect.'

LENDER CONSENT / SUBORDINATION (Secs. 6, 8): the Agreement is at all times subordinate to the LoanCore 2021-CRE6 Issuer Ltd. loan; HFC may pay part of the price by assuming the debt only with holder consent and full release of Owner, Sponsor Member and Guarantors; modifications to the subordination section need Lender's prior written consent. Any acquirer's unwind plan must account for the existing CRE CLO debt.

TRANSFERABILITY: HFC cannot assign its rights (Sec. 7) and the Option/ROFR cannot be transferred without Sponsor Member's sole-discretion consent (Sec. 9) — the rights are personal to Pleasanton HFC (wholly owned subsidiary permitted as acquisition vehicle only). Conversely, Sec. 12 bars ANY party from assigning without the others' consent (not unreasonably withheld).

key_terms: SET-ASIDE (operative covenant, Sec. 2(a)(i), p.3): no less than 175 of the 350 Units (50%) must be reserved for/rented to and occupied by households earning less than 80% of AMI ('80% Low Income Households'), counting combined incomes of all unit occupants. Single AMI tier only — no 60% tier, no income averaging.

RECITAL-LEVEL MISSION STANDARD (p.1): not less than 50% of units for families earning less than 80% AMI per the Act, AND not less than 90% of units reserved for/occupied by 'low and moderate income individuals and families as defined by the HFC' (the 90% covenant appears only in the recitals, not in Section 2's operative Rental Requirement).

AMI DEFINITION (Sec. 1(d), p.2): area median family income for the Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land, TX HUD Metro FMR Area, adjusted for a four (4) person household, calculated per the Novogradac Rent and Income Limit Calculator (the 'Calculator') under the 'Other Federal, State, or Local Program' category. If the Calculator is unavailable, a reasonable substitute tool mutually agreed by the parties and by the indirect members of the Grantor.

RENT CAP FORMULA (Sec. 1(d) p.2; Sec. 2(a)(i) p.3): maximum monthly rent = AMI x 0.80 x 0.35 / 12 (AMI times 80%, times a 35% rent cap, divided by 12 months). Rents set by the Calculator WITHOUT regard to utility allowances; must not exceed 35% of 0.8 x AMI / 12.

AMI DECLINE RATCHET (Sec. 2(b)(i), p.4): if AMI falls year-over-year, Grantor need not reduce rents on Low-Income Units but cannot increase them until AMI rises again; any increase must be consistent with the Calculator.

TERM (Sec. 4, p.5): commences on the Effective Date and ends on the date HFC no longer owns title to the Land or the Project — i.e., the covenants do NOT survive a sale out of HFC ownership; no fixed year term.

TERMINATION — INVOLUNTARY (Sec. 4, pp.5-6): requirements terminate upon involuntary noncompliance caused by fire, seizure, requisition, foreclosure, exercise of power of sale, deed in lieu of foreclosure, condemnation or similar event, or a change in federal law or federal-agency action after the Effective Date preventing HFC enforcement.
TERMINATION — GROUND LEASE (Sec. 4, p.6): automatic termination upon termination or expiration of the Ground Lease.

TERMINATION — MUTUAL (Sec. 4, p.6): HFC and Grantor may agree to terminate; parties to execute/record release instruments, but recording is not a prerequisite to effectiveness; all termination costs (incl. HFC fees/expenses) paid by Grantor and its successors.
VOUCHERS (Sec. 1(g), p.3): no discrimination based on source of income; Project must accept Housing Choice Vouchers.

VOUCHER SUITABILITY CAP (Sec. 1(h), p.3): a Low Income Tenant using an HFC-allocated Housing Choice Voucher need only show monthly income of 2-1/2 times the portion of monthly rent NOT paid by the voucher; confirms the 175 'Low Income Unit(s)' count.

UNIT PARITY (Sec. 1(i), p.3): non-Low-Income Units are 'Market Units'; Low Income Units must be evenly distributed throughout the Project with renovations/furnishings/fixtures/equipment of comparable standard to Market Units.

TEMPORARY OCCURRENCE CURE (Sec. 2(b), pp.3-4): if the Rental Requirement fails due to vacancy, required repairs, or income increase of a tenant, Grantor must restore compliance as soon as possible and in any case within sixty (60) days; no obligation to evict; if <100% occupied, reserve the appropriate proportion; if 100% occupied, lease next available units to Low Income Tenants until 50% of total units are so occupied.
VACANT UNIT RULE (Sec. 2(a), p.3): a vacant unit last occupied by a Low-Income Tenant counts as a Low-Income Unit until reoccupied.

INCOME CERTIFICATIONS (Sec. 2(c), pp.4-5): initial Income Certification dated immediately prior to occupancy for each Low Income Tenant; annual recertification on each occupancy anniversary and no less than every 12 months; plus event-driven recerts on change in family composition or income increase. Verification steps: 4-week pay stubs, 2 years of tax returns, consumer credit search, employer verification, SSA verification, or other independent verification. TDHCA LIHTC certification form permitted as an alternative (Exhibit C is the base form).

REPORTING (Sec. 2(e), p.5): beginning one year after the Effective Date and annually on the anniversary until end of Term, Grantor submits to HFC a Continuing Program Compliance Certificate (Exhibit B form) with an audit report prepared by the Compliance Specialist under the Audit and Compliance Agreement; unit-designation changes reported on the annual certificate filed with HFC and the Compliance Specialist (Sec. 2(b)(ii), p.4).

RECORDS/INSPECTION (Sec. 2(d), p.5): complete and accurate records of Low-Income Units; HFC representatives may inspect books and records at reasonable times on reasonable notice during business hours.

LEASE PROVISIONS (Sec. 2(f), p.5): every Low Income Unit lease must state that material misstatement in the Income Certification (intentional or not) may be cause for immediate lease termination, and disclose annual income recertification.
MARKETING (Sec. 2(h), p.5): market per Grantor's marketing plan; all public marketing materials and websites must reference the Rental Requirement and voucher acceptance in both English and Spanish.
NO MATERIAL MODIFICATION (Sec. 2(b)(ii), p.4): no material modification of the Regulatory Agreement without prior written consent of HFC, Grantor, AND the Compliance Specialist.

COVENANTS RUN WITH LAND (Sec. 5, p.6): covenants run with the land, binding on Grantor's successors and Grantor's leasehold title; BUT expire upon termination of the Regulatory Agreement; every later contract/deed/instrument is conclusively deemed subject to them whether or not recited.
LENDER PROTECTION (Sec. 5, p.6): no breach impairs, defeats, or invalidates the lien of any mortgage/deed of trust made in good faith and for value.

DEFAULT/ENFORCEMENT (Sec. 7, pp.6-7): Event of Default after uncured default 60 days post written notice from HFC; if not curable in 60 days, no Event of Default so long as Grantor (or direct/indirect members) institutes corrective action within 60 days and diligently pursues it — but cure period capped at one hundred twenty (120) days. SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE IS THE SOLE REMEDY ('specific enforcement ... is the only means by which HFC may obtain the benefits'); HFC recovers reasonable legal fees when enforcing an Event of Default.

SUBORDINATION (Sec. 8, p.7): Grantor must record the agreement and all amendments in the Land Records and pay all recording fees; the Regulatory Agreement is subject and subordinate to all matters of record as of its date.

TAX-EXEMPTION DISCLAIMER (Sec. 2(a), p.3): HFC makes NO representation as to qualification for the Chapter 394 ad valorem tax exemption due to occupancy of a Low-Income Unit by a tenant at 80% AMI or above.

MISC (Sec. 9, pp.7-8): Texas governing law (excluding conflicts rules); amendments only by written recorded instrument (subject to Sec. 4); notice by personal/overnight/certified mail, deemed given on delivery/refusal or 3 business days after mailing; severability; counterparts.

verbatim_quotes.text: This Memorandum of Understanding (the "MOU") is between Pleasanton Housing Finance Corporation ("PHFC"), a Texas nonprofit and public facility corporation, and Sarah At Lake Houston SPE LLC, its affiliates, and its assigns ("Developer"), and is effective as of July 1, 2024.
Sarah At Lake Houston Apartments, being a 350-unit multifamily residential rental housing development located in Humble, Harris County, Texas (the "Project").

The PHFC shall then enter into a 99-year ground lease ("Ground Lease") with a limited partnership or a limited liability company (the "Tenant" or the "Partnership") owned by PHFC through a special purpose entity (the "General Partner"), Developer or its affiliate (the "Special LP"), and its equity investor, if and as applicable (the "Investor LP"), as tenant.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the tax-exempt status of the Project is lost for any reason during the first 20 years, other than a default caused by Developer, then fee title to the Project shall be transferred from PHFC to the Tenant or the then existing tenant under the Ground Lease for $1.00.

Within thirty (30) days of its receipt of a Sale Notice, the PHFC, General Partner, Ground Lessor or other PHFC affiliate (the "HFC Entity") shall have a right of first refusal (the "ROFR") to purchase the Partnership Interests or the Project on the same terms and conditions contained in the Sale Notice.

In addition, upon Closing, the PHFC shall have a purchase option (the "Option") to acquire the Project at a price (the "Purchase Price") equal to the sum of (I) fair market value and (II) the sum of (i) an amount, on an after tax basis, equal to the diminution of economic value to the Partnership's limited partners as a result of the purchase of the Partnership's interest in the Project by the PHFC (the "Tenant Diminution"), which shall include without limitation (A) 125% of the aggregate of all capital contributions and any other advances of any made by the partners of the Partnership prior to Closing of the Option

The Ground Lease and Regulatory Agreement will provide that for any year the Tenant wishes to obtain a property tax exemption, it will set aside or rent at least 50% of the units to tenants earning less than 80% of the area median income ("AMI") established by the Department of Housing and Urban Development for the Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land MSA (the "Affordable Units").

The income and rent limits will not be adjusted for family size and will not be calculated with regard to utility allowances; provided, however, that the rents shall not exceed 35% of 0.8 multiplied by the AMI, divided by 12 for the Affordable Units.

If the tax exemption is not issued for the Project, then PHFC shall promptly reconvey the Project to the Tenant for the sum of $10.00 upon written request by the Tenant and shall reimburse to Developer the Closing Fee paid to PHFC at closing.

Furthermore, the Developer and Tenant may choose to voluntarily have the property reconveyed by PHFC at any time for the sum of $10.00 upon written request by the Developer or Tenant, at which point the tax exemption would cease.

PHFC shall be entitled to receive a one-time Closing Fee (the "Closing Fee") for its participation in the Project.  The amount of the Closing Fee for the Project shall be equal to $300,000.00.  Additionally, PHFC or its affiliate acting as general contractor shall receive an amount equal to 25% of any sales tax savings during construction or rehabilitation for the Project for serving as the general contractor pursuant to the Master Subcontract.

Pursuant to the Ground Lease, PHFC shall be entitled to receive an annual fee payable from the Tenant in an amount equal to 10% of the annual ad valorem property tax savings for the Project (the "Savings Fee") determined following, final, non-appealable resolution of any contest of the ad valorem tax values for the Project and paid no later than January 31 of the year following the year in which the applicable property tax would have been owed

An annual compliance fee (the "Annual Compliance Fee") for annual oversight and accountability compliance management functions on behalf of the Tenant in an amount equal to $100.00 per unit per calendar year shall be payable to Affordable Housing Compliance Services, LLC.
This MOU reflects the entire understanding between the parties and may only be amended in writing, signed by both parties.  This MOU is a binding obligation and is not merely an "agreement to agree."

The parties hereto submit exclusively to the jurisdiction of the state and federal courts of Atascosa County, Texas, and venue for any cause of action arising hereunder shall lie exclusively in the state and federal courts of Atascosa County, Texas.
All costs of PHFC Counsel, up to a maximum aggregate amount of $125,000.00, will be considered Costs hereunder and paid as provided herein.
